provenance.canonical-source: THERE IS NO SOURCE. This column is a CONFIRMED ABSENCE, not an unfilled column. shadcn/ui ships no chip, no tag and no pill component. Every row below is `off` and every one carries a citation, because CLAUDE.md law 3 says a silent gap is a failing build and an absence that is merely blank is indistinguishable from one that was never checked. The file exists so the generator emits chip-shadcn.css (the chassis's theme-invariant base layout and nothing else) and so the panel shows an explicit, evidenced 'no' in every cell.
provenance.evidence-1-directory-listing: `ls ui/apps/v4/registry/new-york-v4/ui/` returns 63 files. There is no chip.tsx, no tag.tsx and no pill.tsx. The nearest neighbours in this space are badge.tsx (ALREADY BUILT as its own registry component — docs/BADGE-MATRIX.md), toggle.tsx / toggle-group.tsx (a different canonical row, excluded by the brief) and combobox.tsx (see evidence 3).
provenance.evidence-2-filename-search: `find ui -not -path '*/node_modules/*' \( -iname '*chip*' -o -iname '*pill*' -o -iname '*tag*.tsx' \)` returns NOTHING — not one file in the entire clone is named for any of the three.
provenance.evidence-3-every-chip-string-in-the-clon: `grep -ril chip` across apps/v4 returns exactly four kinds of hit, and every one of them is the chip-INSIDE-A-FIELD pattern the brief excludes by structural reason: (a) registry/new-york-v4/ui/combobox.tsx, which exports ComboboxChips, ComboboxChip, ComboboxChipsInput and renders ComboboxPrimitive.Chip / ComboboxPrimitive.ChipRemove from Base UI's combobox — these are the combobox's own tokenised-input parts, imported from the combobox primitive and exported from the combobox file; (b) the same three exports repeated in registry/bases/{radix,base,aria}/ui/combobox.tsx and consumed by blocks/preview/cards/assign-issue.tsx; (c) registry/styles/style-*.css, eight theme files each carrying a `.cn-combobox-chip` / `.cn-combobox-chips` class — again combobox-scoped; (d) app/(app)/examples/tasks/data/tasks.json, where the word is 'microchip' inside lorem-ipsum task titles. There is no fifth kind of hit.
provenance.evidence-4-documentation: `ls apps/v4/content/docs/components/{radix,base,aria}/` has no chip.mdx, no tag.mdx and no pill.mdx. The only docs page in which the string 'chip' appears is combobox.mdx, in all three bases. The only badge-family docs page is badge.mdx, which belongs to the already-built badge component.
provenance.evidence-5-registry-index: `grep -c 'chip\|pill' apps/v4/registry/new-york-v4/ui/_registry.ts` returns 0. The component is absent from shadcn's own machine-readable index, not merely from the filesystem.
provenance.evidence-6-lesson-11-the-files-are-reada: `file apps/v4/registry/new-york-v4/ui/*.tsx` reports every one of the 63 files as text — none is misclassified as binary. This matters because docs/CARD-MATRIX.md's validation pass found a single NUL byte in skeleton/card.tsx that made the file binary and silently defeated EVERY grep against it, turning a working keyboard handler into an apparent a11y defect. An empty grep is not evidence of absence until the file is known to be text; here the whole directory has been checked, so the empty greps above are evidence.
provenance.corroboration-from-the-registry-itself: docs/COMPONENTS.md line 111 already records this independently: `| tag / pill | — (badge) | ✓ tag, pill | ✓ chip family (assist/filter/input/suggestion) |`. The master component list, written in phase 1 from a separate pass over the three clones, puts a dash in shadcn's cell and names badge as what shadcn has instead. Two independent passes, one answer.
provenance.why-badge-is-not-substituted: shadcn's badge.tsx is the obvious temptation and taking it would be a rule-1 retrofit — one design system's material draped over a component the other two define. It is also double-counting: badge is ALREADY BUILT as its own registry component with its own template, its own three columns, its own skeleton and its own behaviour gate. And the two are not the same thing by either system's own account. Salt's badge/usage.mdx draws the line three times ('To trigger an immediate action ... Instead, use Pill'; 'To communicate status through color ... Instead, use Pill'; 'To communicate read-only metadata ... use Tag'), and Salt's pill/usage.mdx draws it back the other way ('For labeling. Instead, use Tag') as does tag/usage.mdx ('To display counts, notifications ... Instead, use Badge'). A badge is inert, single-coloured and system-driven; a chip is interactive, selectable and user-driven. shadcn simply has no component on the second side of that line.
provenance.what-shadcn-users-actually-do: Recorded so the absence is understood rather than merely stated. For the interactive case shadcn points at toggle / toggle-group (a different canonical row, excluded by the brief for the same structural reason); for the removable-token case it points at ComboboxChip inside a combobox; for the static label case it points at badge. Three different components covering what Salt covers with two and M3 with four. None of them is a chip.

behavior.delete-affordance.value: NO COMPONENT, so shadcn ABSTAINS from the a11y fork. Worth stating explicitly because the fork has only two answers in this registry rather than three: Salt says do-not-nest (the whole pill is the delete control, one tab stop) and M3's spec says nest (a trailing remove button, two tab stops). The nearest shadcn code, ComboboxChipRemove, IS a nested focusable — but it belongs to combobox, on the input-group COMPONENTS.md row, and is excluded by the brief's tokenised-input rule.
